RTR-2Every change the fork makes to an upstream file is one of eleven kinds, and nothing else: clock read or deadline: time.Now, time.Since, time.After or a context deadline becomes the runtime's clock (rt.Now, rt.Clock()); timer or periodic work: a goroutine looping on a ticker becomes rt.Every(ctx, name, interval, fn); goroutine or blocking wait: go f() becomes rt.Go(f); a blocking select becomes rt.Park(condition); random draw: a draw from a global or unseeded source becomes a draw from a named stream, rt.Rand("<name>"); iteration order: when hosted, a map or sync.Map listing that reaches a decision is sorted, or sorted and then shuffled from a named stream; when not hosted, upstream's order is kept; network call: when hosted, an outbound HTTP call goes through hosting.Transport, which the host serves; work ordering: work the upstream runs in parallel or in the background runs, when hosted, one item at a time in a fixed order; when not hosted, upstream's concurrency is kept; per-simulation state: state the upstream shares across the whole process, such as the picker's tie-break counter or random source, is kept per runtime when hosted (rt.Local), so two simulations in one process do not share it; hosted substitute: when hosted, a component is replaced by one with the same contract that the host can drive, such as a time-to-live cache on the runtime's clock, or a path BLIS does not host is refused by name; test adaptation: an upstream test is changed only to follow a signature another allowed kind changed; startup assembly: the runner is split so a host can build the router without servers, Kubernetes reconcilers or leader election.newM3the fork changes 36 upstream Go files (273 lines added, 143 removed) at v1.0.0-blis.2; most changes are of a listed kind, four hunks are not (prerequest_test.go, handlers/request.go, producer.go, handlers/response.go); today a 450-line budget is checked instead
